title: OVHcloud SBG2 Strasbourg Data-Center Fire (10 March 2021)
text: In the early hours of 10 March 2021 a fire broke out in a ground-floor energy room at OVHcloud's SBG2 facility in Strasbourg, where the site's UPS units and their lead-acid battery banks were housed. Video surveillance and the fire panel traced the initiating event to a near-simultaneous electrical fault on UPS2 and its connected batteries. With no automatic suppression system in any of the five campus buildings, and a free-cooling design that used intumescent-treated raw-wood floors and single-skin cladding to aid airflow, the fire spread through the entire structure. De-energisation was slow because there was no accessible general site cut-off, forcing the grid operator to isolate an upstream substation; current was still present in the burning building well after the cut order. SBG2 was destroyed in its entirety, four of twelve rooms in adjacent SBG1 were partially destroyed, and the SBG2–SBG3 inter-building link was impacted. Roughly 30,000 servers were lost and about 3.6 million websites went offline. There were no casualties or injuries. French investigator BEA-RI could establish the fault location but not its precise cause, leaving several hypotheses open pending a court-expert examination.

title: OVHcloud SBG2 Strasbourg Data-Center Fire (10 March 2021)
text: The fire originated on the ground floor of SBG2 in the energy room complex housing the UPS units and their lead-acid battery banks. Video surveillance and the site fire-control panel establish an electrical fault at UPS2 and at the batteries connected to it (the two were in separate rooms), with fire outbreaks appearing almost simultaneously on the batteries and on an inverter. The precise cause of the UPS failure could not be established by BEA-RI; candidate hypotheses include liquid or humidity from the nearby cooling system, a fault linked to a maintenance operation performed the same morning, or operation of the inverter outside its normal ranges. The ambiguity is deepened by the use of lead-acid (not lithium) batteries, which BEA-RI characterises as more robust and stable, with internal short circuits being rare. The precise ignition mechanism was left to an ongoing court-expert examination.

title: OVHcloud SBG2 Strasbourg Data-Center Fire (10 March 2021)
text: The initiating event sits in the UPS/battery topology of SBG2's ground-floor energy rooms. BEA-RI's forensic basis is the site's own video surveillance and fire-control panel telemetry, which localise an electrical fault to UPS2 and to the lead-acid battery string connected to it — with the UPS and its batteries deliberately sited in separate rooms. Fire outbreaks registered almost simultaneously on the batteries and on an inverter, indicating the fault propagated across the charging chain rather than being confined to a single component. SBG2's battery population was substantial: 800 lead-acid units of roughly 30 kg and 13 kW unit power each. Because lead-acid chemistry is comparatively stable and internal shorts are rare, BEA-RI could not close out the ignition cause and enumerated three non-exclusive hypotheses — ingress of liquid/humidity from the physically adjacent cooling system, a defect introduced by the maintenance operation performed the same morning, or operation of the inverter outside its qualified envelope — deferring the definitive determination to a court-expert. The decisive engineering weakness was the response envelope, not merely the fault. With detection but no automatic suppression, and no local general cut-off, the facility could not be made electrically safe fast enough to permit water: the cut order at 00:58 propagated only to the upstream SER (Strasbourg Électricité Réseaux) source substation effective at 01:50, yet 02:14 telemetry showed SBG2 still energised and fire spreading to SBG1, and full de-energisation was achieved only at 03:28. In parallel, the water side was undersized — one hydrant below 60 m3/h, no on-site reserve, and no Rhine-canal pumping means — so effective flow depended on the fireboat. The building fabric closed the loop: intumescent-treated raw-wood floors and single-skin/aluminium cladding, engineered for free-cooling heat exchange, provided combustible vertical pathways and negligible compartmentation. The net systemic failure mode is the coincidence of a low-probability power-electronics fault with an environment offering no independent means of early suppression, rapid isolation, or adequate water — the hallmark of insufficient defence-in-depth around the energy plant.

text: Cross-incident pattern: single-facility concentration and thin defence-in-depth: SBG2 is a canonical example of correlated failure: tens of thousands of servers and millions of dependent websites concentrated in one building whose defensive layers — suppression, compartmentation, rapid de-energisation, and water supply — were all thin or absent simultaneously, so a single power-room fault removed everything at once. The recurring lesson mirrors other large outages: efficiency and cost optimisations that quietly erode independent safety layers, plus customer over-reliance on a single site without geo-redundant backups, turn a contained component fault into a headline loss. Resilience here was ultimately proven not by the facility's own defences but by cross-site failover and industrial replacement capacity.
